ache and neuralgia, left side. Took Nitric acid without relief (seventh

Eye. —[30.] Eyes dry and itching, nearly every evening, rubs them,
without giving relief (fifth day),'.—While walking, pain around left eye,

beard (sixth day),'.—Since several days, and particularly noticeable to-day,

Thvoat. —[40.] Frequently hawks up small solid lumps of phlegm,

StOTtiach .—Aversion to beer (eighth to eleventh day),'.—Several times
tasteless eructations between 10 and 11 a.m. (after half an hour),'.—Sev¬
eral times eructations, the last one leaving a sourish taste in the mouth
(soou),^—Violent pain, like the digging with the end of a stick, in right
side, two or three inches to the right of the epigastrium, where the eighth
and ninth ribs ascend to the sternum ; then pressing pain under the ribs,

A-bdonien .—Pain and soreness in the liver (seventh day),®.—Frequent
passage of small quantities of odorless flatus (third day),'.—Frequent pas¬
sages of unusually small and short flatus (sixth day),'.—[50.] Bellyache be¬
fore rising (third day),^—Pain in the abdomen, particularly in the region

bles pressed forcibly upward through the intestines. The stitches and the

the above-mentioned stitches returned, but were of short duration. They
returned several times, first on the left side, then less severe on the right.
Often but single stitches, or, more accurately, bites, as if an animal were
snapping and tearing off little bits from the inside. Flatuleney and dis¬
tension of the abdomen. Sensation as if the intestines were strangulated
and twisted in different directions, more in the upper than lower portion.
Frequent passage of flatus. Painful stitches in the left side, followed by
cutting, more right than left side, almost unbearable, lasting some min¬
utes; returns after a short interval and lasts longer (first day). Stitches
in the abdomen (second day). Unpleasant sensation in the groins, painful
to pressure, feeling as if emptied of viscera (third day). The prover had
no more symptoms of tapeworm for more than a year afterwards,'.—Ach¬
ing in the left groin at every step (seventh day),®;

Itectiini and Anns .—At the apjn-oach of a stool, dull stitches, or

(Of a constipated habit for years, the stools now became soft,
and remained so until after the proving, when again constipation as be¬
fore),’. First a hard, then a mushy, thin stool, with protrusion of the anus,

JJvinavy Orf/nas .—Pressing pain in region of left kidney, as if the

ney (fifth day),®.—Pressing in the bladder, as if it were full of urine (first

ing to urinate and scanty discharge remain (third day),*.

Sejcual Ovyans .—Erections every morning, but none in the even¬
ing and at night, even none from excitation (eighth to eleventh day),’.—
Pain in uterus or region of the bladder (fifth day),®.— In the evening she

eral days sooner,®.

Generalities. —Very tired in the evening (thirteenth day)/.—[120.]
Very tired when walking, he reels on coming into the room, in the even¬
ing (third day),h—Feels heavy, tired in the limbs, inert, and undecided, in
the morning (third day),'.—Aversion to making any exertion. She feels
as after taking Mercury and afterwards Magnesia, as she has sometimes
done, but this may have been caused by the exertion (seventh day),®.—
While walking it seems to him as if he had grown much taller; the feel¬

side (forgotten because it disappeared on turning), a peculiar pain never

there (first day),\—Bellyache before rising, afterwards pain in right tem¬

.shoulder and arm, then again in right temple. Some pain in small of back,
extending over the right thigh, then pain in right wrist, in left hip, right
hand, and right lower jaw. After a walk, at noon, pain in right temple
and right arm. The pains change place so quickly, and at times are so

Skin, —Small pimples on various places, particularly back of the left

the whole body, while undressing, in the evening (sixth day),'.—At 1 A.M.,
